answer: Witness-linked anchoring. Each identity periodically signs a challenge whose kernel is unpredictably assigned to a fixed public location tied to a verifiable offline record, and the identity must confirm a neighboring witness was physically at that anchor at that moment. Identities forced onto the same sparse witness pool under tundra-like low-density conditions reveal shared witnesses across purportedly independent agents. Duplicating identities then requires distinct real-world witnesses per clone, a costly recurring physical-presence expense.
